primaryGoal: Identify the top 3 worst performing Campaign Categories based on the highest M0 to M1 opportunity drop for the current month, and for each of these categories, identify the specific campaigns (Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name) with the highest drop.
assumptions: The [Opportunity M0 Date] and [Opportunity M1 Date] fields accurately reflect when opportunities were created at each stage.
The current month filter applies to both M0 and M1 dates independently, meaning we analyze opportunities that reached M0 this month and opportunities that reached M1 this month separately.
A higher drop (M0 count minus M1 count) indicates worse performance, suggesting poor conversion or progression from M0 to M1 stage.
The filters [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', and [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode' apply consistently across all data fetches.
All required data for both Campaign Category and Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name analysis will be fetched upfront to enable comprehensive analysis without additional data retrieval.

phases.phaseDescription: Fetch all M0 opportunity data for the current month at the most granular level (Campaign Category and Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name) to enable comprehensive drop analysis. This phase captures the starting point of the funnel.

fetchSteps.title: Fetch 1: M0 Opportunity Counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name
fetchSteps.objective: Retrieve all M0 opportunity counts for the current month, grouped by both Campaign Category and specific Campaign Name, with all required filters applied.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Columns: [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]. Filters: [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode', [Opportunity M0 Date] = current month. Aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] grouped by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: Fetch all opportunities where [Opportunity M0 Date] is in the current month and [Opportunity Source] equals 'marketing' and [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] equals 'digital and events' and [Opportunity Deployment] does not equal 'mode'. Include columns [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], and the sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]. Group the results by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 1: Aggregate M0 Counts by Campaign Category
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the total M0 opportunity count for each Campaign Category in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [Campaign Category] and calculate the total sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] for each category. Present the results as a table showing Campaign Category and their corresponding M0 totals. This will serve as the baseline for identifying drop performance.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 2: Aggregate M0 Counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name
analysisSteps.groupBy: [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name]
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the M0 opportunity count for each specific Campaign Name within each Campaign Category?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, maintain the granular grouping by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name] and present the sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] for each combination. Create a detailed table showing Campaign Category, Campaign Name, and M0 counts. This granular view will be used for drill-down analysis.

phases.phaseDescription: Fetch all M1 opportunity data for the current month at the same granular level (Campaign Category and Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name) to enable direct comparison with M0 data. This phase captures the progression point in the funnel.

fetchSteps.title: Fetch 2: M1 Opportunity Counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name
fetchSteps.objective: Retrieve all M1 opportunity counts for the current month, grouped by both Campaign Category and specific Campaign Name, with all required filters applied.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Columns: [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]. Filters: [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode', [Opportunity M1 Date] = current month. Aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] grouped by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: Fetch all opportunities where [Opportunity M1 Date] is in the current month and [Opportunity Source] equals 'marketing' and [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] equals 'digital and events' and [Opportunity Deployment] does not equal 'mode'. Include columns [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], and the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]. Group the results by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 3: Aggregate M1 Counts by Campaign Category
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the total M1 opportunity count for each Campaign Category in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [Campaign Category] and calculate the total sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] for each category. Present the results as a table showing Campaign Category and their corresponding M1 totals. This will be compared with M0 data to calculate drop metrics.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 4: Aggregate M1 Counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name
analysisSteps.groupBy: [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name]
analysisSteps.aggregation: Sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the M1 opportunity count for each specific Campaign Name within each Campaign Category?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, maintain the granular grouping by [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name] and present the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] for each combination. Create a detailed table showing Campaign Category, Campaign Name, and M1 counts. This granular view will be used for campaign-level drop analysis.

phases.phaseDescription: Calculate the M0 to M1 drop for each Campaign Category by comparing the M0 data from Phase 1 with M1 data from Phase 2. Identify the top 3 Campaign Categories with the highest absolute drop, representing the worst performing categories.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis 5: Calculate M0 to M1 Drop by Campaign Category
fetchSteps.objective: Compute the absolute drop (M0 - M1) and drop percentage for each Campaign Category to identify worst performers.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Use outputs from Analysis 1.1.1 (M0 counts by Campaign Category) and Analysis 2.1.1 (M1 counts by Campaign Category).
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new data fetch required. This analysis uses previously fetched data from steps 1.1.1 and 2.1.1.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 5: Identify Top 3 Worst Performing Campaign Categories
analysisSteps.aggregation: Calculated metric: M0_to_M1_Drop = (M0 Count - M1 Count)
analysisSteps.question: Which are the top 3 Campaign Categories with the highest absolute drop from M0 to M1 in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the M0 counts from Analysis 1.1.1 and M1 counts from Analysis 2.1.1, join the datasets on [Campaign Category]. For each Campaign Category, calculate: (1) Absolute Drop = M0 Count - M1 Count, (2) Drop Percentage = ((M0 Count - M1 Count) / M0 Count) * 100. Sort the results by Absolute Drop in descending order and identify the top 3 Campaign Categories with the highest drop. Present a table with columns: Campaign Category, M0 Count, M1 Count, Absolute Drop, Drop Percentage. Highlight the top 3 worst performers and provide a brief insight on the magnitude of the drop for each.

phases.phaseDescription: For each of the top 3 worst performing Campaign Categories identified in Phase 3, drill down to the individual Campaign Name level to identify which specific campaigns contributed most to the poor performance. This provides actionable insights for targeted intervention.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis 6: Calculate M0 to M1 Drop by Campaign Name within Top 3 Categories
fetchSteps.objective: For each of the top 3 Campaign Categories, calculate the M0 to M1 drop at the Campaign Name level to identify the worst performing individual campaigns.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Use outputs from Analysis 1.1.2 (M0 counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name) and Analysis 2.1.2 (M1 counts by Campaign Category and Campaign Name), filtered for only the top 3 Campaign Categories identified in Analysis 3.1.1.
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new data fetch required. This analysis uses previously fetched granular data from steps 1.1.2 and 2.1.2, filtered for the top 3 Campaign Categories.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 6: Identify Worst Performing Campaigns within Each Top 3 Category
analysisSteps.groupBy: [Campaign Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name]
analysisSteps.aggregation: Calculated metric: M0_to_M1_Drop = (M0 Count - M1 Count)
analysisSteps.question: For each of the top 3 worst performing Campaign Categories, which specific Campaign Names (Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name) had the highest M0 to M1 drop?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the granular M0 counts from Analysis 1.1.2 and M1 counts from Analysis 2.1.2, join the datasets on [Campaign Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name]. Filter the joined dataset to include only the top 3 Campaign Categories identified in Analysis 3.1.1. For each Campaign Name within these categories, calculate: (1) Absolute Drop = M0 Count - M1 Count, (2) Drop Percentage = ((M0 Count - M1 Count) / M0 Count) * 100. For each of the top 3 Campaign Categories, sort the Campaign Names by Absolute Drop in descending order and identify the campaign(s) with the highest drop. Present the results in three separate sections (one for each top Campaign Category), showing: Campaign Category, Campaign Name, M0 Count, M1 Count, Absolute Drop, Drop Percentage. Provide insights on which specific campaigns are underperforming within each category and the severity of their drop.

phases.phaseDescription: Synthesize findings from all previous phases to provide a comprehensive summary of the worst performing campaigns and actionable recommendations for improvement.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis 7: Synthesize Final Insights
fetchSteps.objective: Consolidate all findings into a coherent narrative that answers the primary business goal and provides clear next steps.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Use all outputs from Phases 3 and 4.
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new data fetch required. This is a synthesis analysis using all previous analysis outputs.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 7: Generate Executive Summary and Recommendations
analysisSteps.question: What is the complete picture of campaign underperformance, and what specific actions should be taken?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Synthesize all findings from Phases 3 and 4 to create an executive summary that includes: (1) A clear statement of the top 3 worst performing Campaign Categories with their drop metrics, (2) For each of these categories, the specific Campaign Names that are driving the poor performance, (3) The business impact of these drops in terms of lost opportunities from M0 to M1, (4) Actionable recommendations such as: pausing or optimizing underperforming campaigns, investigating root causes (targeting, messaging, channel effectiveness), reallocating budget from worst performers to better performers, and setting up monitoring for early detection of similar drops. Present this as a structured executive summary with clear sections for Findings, Impact, and Recommendations.
